newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet names industry veteran as president, CEO.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet names industry veteran as president, CEO.

text.p: ValuJet Inc., which restructured itself last month into a holding company, announced several executive changes Monday, including the appointment of industry veteran Joseph Corr as president and chief executive of its airline unit.

ValuJet, which reorganized to make the airline a wholly owned subsidiary of ValuJet Inc. on Oct. 20, said Robert L. Priddy would become chairman of the parent company while Lewis H. Jordan would become chairman of the airline.

The company, which is still working to return to full service after a fatal crash in May, said that Jordan will remain president and chief operating officer of the holding company as well as assuming the position of chairman of the airline subsidiary, ValuJet Airlines Inc.
"These organisational changes add significant strength to an already strong airline team and facilitate development of other holding company interests," Priddy said in a statement.
The company said Priddy will devote full time to his position as chairman and CEO of the holding company.

ValuJet, which returned to the skies Sept. 30 after being grounded for most of the summer following the May crash that killed 110 people, said Corr would take over as the airline's president and chief executive Wednesday.
Corr, 55, previously served as chairman, president, chief executive and director of Continental Airlines and as president, vice chairman and director of Trans World Airlines.

"Joe Corr, in his new position, will provide excellent leadership in taking ValuJet Airlines to the next level of operational excellence as we continue our development and growth," Jordan said in a statement.
ValuJet's stock added 12.5 cents to $9.875 in morning trading on the Nasdaq market.
